[h3]Half-finished and laughably bad[/h3] 

If this was from an indie studio, I would give a more optimistic review; however, this is from Microsoft, so I'll do no such thing.

I'll start with the combat. It feels floaty. I tried adjusting the sensitivity, dead zones, aim assist, etc., but nothing I tried seemed to help. It almost felt like the gameplay settings were added in the last moments before release and don't actually adjust anything. They are just for show. 

And then there's the enemy AI. It's terrible. I have played indie games from 10 years ago that put this game to shame. Also, in just 1 hour of gameplay, I had 2 separate encounters with enemies that were invisible. I had to run away and bait them to chase me until they eventually popped into the game and I could shoot them.

The story makes little sense; they brush over important questions that anyone would have when first introduced to a new game/world. 'Don't think, just consume content' seems to be the developers' mantra.  

The idea behind this game has potential, and the style they went for is also appealing to me, but there's no soul here. No passion. No talent. 

⠀

Decent game. The story is pretty simple, but the atmosphere is great. Sadly, it starts with a major UI bug, just as you try to start the game for the first time. There are also the occasional crashes, but I've definitely seen worse. 
If you find it on sale and you give it a chance, it'll surprise you!

This game while not a great, is not even close to as bad as other people claim it is. It is basically a watered down Borderlands copy. The story itself is somewhat interesting, gunplay feels smooth, and is not filled with non-stop side mission unlike other games of recent times. I honestly would recommend getting it on a deep discount (under 20$) and giving it a fair shot. I had one crash in all my playtime, and that was it. I think people were way too harsh when this released personally.
